title: Release rhythm ladder and microtrim decision canvas
creator: Isabella Huang
description: Goal: Introduce a lightweight, calendar-aware governance layer (the 'release rhythm ladder') and an accompanying microtrim decision canvas to speed cycle-level scope decisions while minimizing cross-team disruption. This ticket captures the proposal, trade-offs, implementation plan for Q2 pilots, and the acceptance criteria for rollout. The intent is to: 1) make decommit/de-scope decisions predictable and auditable, 2) provide clear, metric-driven triggers for microtrims, and 3) reduce meeting overhead by documenting a one-page decision canvas per candidate trim.
background: Recent cycles show oscillation between overcommitment (teams >95% utilization) and conservative pipeline padding that slows feature delivery. Stakeholder feedback (Growth, Infra, Enterprise) requested clearer gates for decommit that 1) avoid last-minute scope loss for high-impact work and 2) enable systematic small-scope trims for low-value items. Existing playbooks are heavy; this proposal aims for a 10–15 min decision canvas + async signoff pattern.
metrics_and_triggers: Team capacity utilization > 85% for two consecutive sprints -> create microtrim candidate list
Unplanned work ratio > 15% (incidents/urgent bugs) -> reserve 10% cycle buffer next cycle
OKR confidence score < 60% at mid-cycle review -> escalate to ladder step 2 (canary partial decommit)
decision_canvas_template: One-page fields: Candidate (epic/ticket list), Impact on OKRs (high/med/low), Time-to-complete (weeks), Cross-team dependencies, Rollback cost, Customer-visible risk, Suggested microtrim (remove/deferral-slice/minimal scope cut), Required approvers (PM/Eng/SRE/Design), Rationale summary (1–2 lines), Timestamp & signoffs.
tradeoffs: Speed vs. fairness: Faster async trims may disadvantage teams with long lead tasks; mitigated via 'grace window' and pre-declare immutable core work
Centralization vs. autonomy: Ladder enforces cadence but keeps final signoff with PM+Eng leads for each team
Conservatism vs. delivery: Setting trigger thresholds too low will cause excessive trimmings; thresholds tuned conservatively in pilot
decisions: Adopt 3-step ladder: 0 (Informal negotiation), 1 (Microtrim canvas + async signoff within 48h), 2 (Canary partial decommit + reallocation), escalated to 3 (Executive arbitration) only when OKR impact is high
Pilot runs in two orgs (Platform and Integrations) for cycles 2026-Q2, after which we iterate on thresholds and canvas fields

Cross-org dependencies not fully represented in current tooling—mitigation: link canvas to dependency board and require dependency owner signoff
Tooling overhead for signoffs could slow decisions—mitigation: build a minimal Slack workflow for 48h async signoff in pilot
